record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are present. The listed source and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a behavioral comparison of a released abliterated model and its base model, testing refusal removal and capability with a weight-edited artifact rather than measuring or intervening on the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The README reports results for an already-abliterated model, but says this repository contains no weight-modification code and does no activation-level analysis. Its values used to describe the models and prompts are not separate result rows. The harmful-content rates use the README's corrected figures; the README also reports lower raw judge labels for three abliterated responses.
record.test_reason: The study compares a released abliterated Qwen3.5-9B artifact with its matched base on harmful and political prompts. This directly bears on V2, whether a weight-edited ablation removes refusal in a released model. It is behavioural only: no direction is measured, ablated or added, so V1 and V3–V8 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes the edit removed harm guardrails completely (0/10 to 10/10 corrected) and most China-specific censorship (4/12 to 10/12), with capability unchanged at this scale. The author's prediction that capability would degrade was wrong. The author stresses the work is behavioural, not mechanistic. The asymmetry suggests political conditioning may be partly encoded outside the refusal direction, possibly as missing knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluation repository, not a replication of the original activation-level procedure: it compares a released abliterated artifact with its base model, without measuring the direction or implementing the weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports that sampled responses can vary between runs because no sampling seed is exposed; it expects the overall pattern rather than every prompt outcome to reproduce.

fits_no_version.finding: The abliterated model and its base both scored 11/14 on a verifiable-answer capability benchmark.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A released abliterated artifact keeps general capability equal to its base at the 9B scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Both models answered 8/8 non-Chinese political control prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reduction in political non-answers after abliteration is specific to the state-restricted set, not a general change in political answering.

record.problems: The README reports only one 9.7B model pair, 44 prompts total, 4–12 prompts per category, and a single non-deterministic run per prompt. It notes that individual answers can flip across runs. The judge under-reported compliance on three harmful responses; the README gives corrected and raw category figures. The repository does not perform activation-level analysis, and the README says abliteration pipelines may edit several directions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the results reported in the README. The listed result files were not inspected, so no additional results are inferred from their presence.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added. Capability preservation is measured only for a released edited artifact.
The edit procedure itself (which directions or layers huihui_ai ablated) is not inspected. Only one model pair at 9B with Q4_K_M quantisation is tested.
Not tested; the author only speculates that several directions may be ablated.
Not tested. The idea that political conditioning comes from training data is speculation, not a measurement.

missing.what: Dual-use security (over-refusal) category E: both base and abliterated answered 8/8. The benign category D (6 prompts) is described as a sanity check, with no per-model counts given.
Run-to-run instability: the same model answered Tiananmen on one run and deflected on another. Per-prompt outcomes are not stable.
missing.locator: README, Your numbers will differ slightly

record.verdict_notes: The record's rows_left_out claims nothing was left out, but category E results (8/8 both) are not recorded. All results come from one 9.7B pair, 44 prompts, and one non-deterministic run each. The harmful-category values depend on the author's correction of the LLM judge. The base model's political 'answers' sometimes assert state positions, so 'answered' is a loose measure for the political rows.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured or ablated in this repository; no direction-addition intervention is tested.
No ablation or weight-edit procedure is implemented or inspected here; the repository evaluates an already-public abliterated artifact.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
No activation geometry or number of refusal directions is measured; the README's proposed explanation for the political results is speculative.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct direction transfer is tested.
No refusal-training method or training stage is varied.
